sentences.zh: 嗯，在劳动节前的那个周五，总统与他的高级国家安全顾问坐在战情室里，讨论是否要

sentences.zh: 与塔利班达成和平。

sentences.zh: 他的政府已经与这些我们自 9·11 事件以来一直在战斗的武装分子进行了近一年的谈判。

sentences.zh: 而在那一刻，在那个房间里，他面临着一个选择。

sentences.en: Do you go ahead and make peace with them or not?
sentences.zh: 你是继续与他们达成和平，还是不达成？

sentences.en: On the one side was Mike
sentences.zh: 一边是迈克·

sentences.zh: 如果你想按照你所说的那样撤出 5600 名士兵，你可以自己做，而不必与

sentences.zh: 多年来，我们在失败的政客和失败的、彻底失败的外交政策领导下，陷入了无休止的战争和冲突之中。

sentences.en: Yeah, he had said that he wanted to end these endless wars, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，他曾说过他想结束这些无休止的战争，对吧？

sentences.en: That Iraq and Afghanistan, Syria, and all these other places we have troops around the world, that the American public was tired of it.
sentences.zh: 伊拉克、阿富汗、叙利亚，以及我们在世界各地驻军的所有其他地方，美国公众已经厌倦了这一切。

sentences.en: We spent too much money, lost too many lives, and for nothing.
sentences.zh: 我们花了太多的钱，失去了太多的生命，却一无所获。

sentences.en: If we didn't do anything with Iraq, if we never went there, if our presidents went to the beach, we'd be much better off.
sentences.zh: 如果我们没有在伊拉克做任何事，如果我们从未去过那里，如果我们的总统们都去海滩度假，我们会好得多。

sentences.en: If they just went every single day to the beach.

sentences.en: Now, that's a very radically different view than the conventional Republican view up until that point, as represented by George W.
sentences.zh: 这与乔治·W·

sentences.en: Republican Party, including John Bolton.

sentences.en: I mean, these negotiations led by the U.S.

sentences.zh: 为什么美国

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: Hmm.

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: That's a good question.

sentences.en: and called to defend freedom.

sentences.en: After 9-11, George W.
sentences.zh: 9·11 事件后，时任总统乔治·W·

sentences.zh: 布什对当时阿富汗的执政者塔利班说：

sentences.zh: 你们必须把奥萨马·本·拉登交给我们，你们必须把基地组织交给我们，并将他们从你们的国家驱逐出去。

sentences.zh: 这些要求不容谈判或讨论。

sentences.en: Well, we're kind of circling back to that now same position 18 years later.
sentences.zh: 嗯，18 年后的今天，我们又回到了同样的立场。

sentences.en: And a lot of blood and treasure under the bridge between 2001 and 2019.

sentences.en: So what does President Trump decide to do in that room dealing with these warring advisors?

sentences.en: Well, he's not convinced by John Bolton's argument, but he doesn't make a decision to go forward yet either.

sentences.en: The idea of making peace in Afghanistan after all his time in Washington was very appealing to him.
sentences.zh: 在华盛顿度过这段时间后，在阿富汗实现和平的想法对他非常有吸引力。

sentences.en: Now, Camp David, of course, has a historic legacy.
sentences.zh: 当然，戴维营有着历史性的遗产。

sentences.en: It's where Ike and FDR and Reagan used to relax.
sentences.zh: 那是艾森豪威尔、罗斯福和里根曾经放松的地方。

sentences.en: When we first arrived at Camp David, the first thing upon which we agreed was to ask the people of the world to pray that our negotiations would be successful.
sentences.zh: 当我们第一次到达戴维营时，我们达成一致的第一件事就是请求全世界的人民祈祷我们的谈判能够成功。

sentences.en: And where Jimmy Carter made peace between Egypt and Israel.
sentences.zh: 也是吉米·卡特在埃及和以色列之间实现和平的地方。

sentences.en: Those prayers have been answered far beyond any expectations.
sentences.zh: 那些祈祷得到了远超预期的回应。

sentences.en: We have an opportunity to bring about a just and enduring end to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.
sentences.zh: 我们有机会为以巴冲突带来一个公正和持久的终结。

sentences.en: Bill Clinton tried to make peace between Israel and the Palestinians there.
sentences.zh: 比尔·克林顿曾试图在那里促成以色列和巴勒斯坦之间的和平。

sentences.en: Of course, there is no guarantee of success.
sentences.zh: 当然，没有任何成功的保证。

sentences.en: But not to try is to guarantee failure.
sentences.zh: 但不去尝试就等于保证失败。

sentences.en: I've asked the highest levels of our government to come to discuss the current tragedy that has so deeply affected our nation.
sentences.zh: 我已经要求我们政府的最高层前来讨论这场深深影响了我们国家的当前悲剧。

sentences.en: George W.
sentences.zh: 乔治·W·

sentences.en: Bush set the path of the war that we were talking about now in Afghanistan there at Camp David.
sentences.zh: 布什就是在戴维营为我们现在谈论的阿富汗战争设定了道路。

sentences.en: We will not only deal with those who dare attack America, we will deal with those who harbor them and feed them and house them.
sentences.zh: 我们不仅要对付那些胆敢攻击美国的人，我们还要对付那些窝藏、供养和收留他们的人。

sentences.en: So it's a place with a real resonance.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个有着真正共鸣的地方。

sentences.en: It's special.
sentences.zh: 它很特别。

sentences.en: The idea that you would invite the leaders of this band of terrorists, that's what they're designated by the United States government,
sentences.zh: 邀请这群恐怖分子的领导人（这就是美国政府对他们的定性）到马里兰州的群山之中，实际上是在这个特殊的场合接待他们，这确实让一些人觉得是个坏主意。

sentences.en: to the mountains of Maryland, in effect host them in this special setting, really struck some as a bad idea.
sentences.zh: 特别是约翰·博尔顿。

sentences.zh: 但总统坚持推进。

sentences.en: He loved this idea and he began pushing it forward so that they began even telling the Afghan government about a plane coming to pick up the president of Afghanistan, Ashraf Ghani.
sentences.zh: 关键是，我不认为塔利班的想法和总统的想法完全一样，对吧？

sentences.en: The trick is, I don't think the Taliban had necessarily the same idea that the president had, right?
sentences.zh: 塔利班说，我们愿意来，但要在协议宣布之后。

sentences.en: In other words, they wanted the assurance that it was done before they traveled to the heart of the enemy, the United States, and showed up at an event with President Trump.
sentences.zh: 这与特朗普的想法存在根本分歧。

sentences.en: That's a fundamental disagreement with what Trump thought.
sentences.zh: 特朗普想做的是成为交易撮合者。

sentences.zh: 他想成为最终达成交易的人，或者至少被视为达成交易的人。

sentences.en: this remarkable idea for how to finalize an agreement that hadn't yet been fully finalized.

sentences.en: Peter, besides the fact that the president wants to invite the Taliban to Camp David,

sentences.en: from talking to our colleagues is that the Taliban feels really strongly about these being negotiations with the U.S.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是这样。

sentences.en: to end the war, and then it will negotiate with the government of Afghanistan, which, by the way, it views as illegitimate.
